citation: Thompson, D.W. (1917) On Growth and Form, Ch. XVII, pp. ~724-735, Figs. 353-358; Dürer profiles Figs. 364, 366 (pp. ~740-742)
claim_text: Human (and animal) heads/faces and proportions, in the Durer/Camper tradition, are mutually transformable by coordinate deformation; differences of facial angle/proportion are whole-grid deformations.

equations.E2_horizontal_compress: (x, y) ↦ (k x, y) with k ∈ (0,1] — Fig. 354 bone panels A→C
equations.E3_shear: (x, y) ↦ (x + m y, y) — Fig. 357 / 366 oblique Dürer grids
equations.E4_tps: Bookstein thin-plate spline T minimizing bending energy subject to landmark pairs
equations.E5_camper_facial_angle: φ = angle between vector PRO→NAS and Frankfort horizontal ORBI→POR (degrees)

state_variables.grid_levels: Four equidistant horizontals on Dürer frame (chin, nasal base, brow, crown) — Fig. 364

boundary_conditions.frame: Landmarks normalised to unit bounding box of Fig. 364 panel
boundary_conditions.Frankfort: POR and ORBI define horizontal reference for φ

empirical_claims: Three Dürer-derived profile types (Fig. 364) differ by whole-grid repositioning of features on equidistant horizontals.
Camper facial angle indexes a global shear of the profile grid (footnote p. 742).
Affine/TPS maps between digitised Dürer profiles should outperform label-shuffled nulls (whole-form, not independent parts).
